skill.name: sharing-skills
skill.description: Guides contributors through preparing, committing, pushing, and opening a pull request for broadly useful AI skills.
skill.summary: Share tested AI skills upstream through a Git and GitHub pull request workflow.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: The skill is a transparent Git and GitHub contribution workflow guide. Static command, filesystem, and network hits are Markdown examples, GitHub documentation links, and the expected local skills directory. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration intent, or separate binary payload was found.

remediation.issue: Bundled archive duplicates the source skill file and triggers binary review.
remediation.suggestion: Remove SKILL.zip from marketplace submissions when the Markdown source is already present.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance suggests force pushing a branch.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer force-with-lease language and remind users to update only their own contribution branch.

content.value_statement: Contributors need a repeatable way to submit useful skills upstream. This skill provides a Git and GitHub pull request workflow for tested skill changes.
actual_capabilities: Guides contributors through syncing main, creating branches, committing changes, pushing branches, and opening pull requests.
Defines criteria for sharing a skill or keeping it personal.
Provides example commit and pull request message structures.
Explains post-merge cleanup for local and remote branches.
Lists troubleshooting steps for GitHub CLI, SSH authentication, existing skills, and merge conflicts.
limitations: Assumes a local skills repository and an authenticated GitHub CLI are already available.
Does not create or validate the skill content itself.
Uses placeholder upstream repository names that contributors must replace.
Includes command examples that should be reviewed before use in a real repository.

use_cases.title: Contribute a New Skill
use_cases.description: Prepare one tested skill for upstream review with a clear branch, commit, and pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Contribution Flow
use_cases.description: Use a consistent checklist for skill submissions before maintainers review them.

use_cases.title: Prepare Team Submissions
use_cases.description: Help team members separate personal skills from broadly reusable skills before opening PRs.

prompt_templates.title: Decide Whether to Share
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me decide whether to share my skill. Ask about scope, testing, sensitive information, and audience before recommending next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the Contribution Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a contribution plan for my skill named [skill name]. Check branch status, sync main, and show commands before running them.

prompt_templates.title: Draft PR Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a commit message and pull request body for [skill name] using my summary, testing notes, and context. Exclude sensitive details.

prompt_templates.title: Review Upstream Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my prepared skill contribution for upstream readiness. Check changed files, branch state, PR description, testing evidence, and merge conflict risk.

output_examples.input: I built a reusable testing skill and want to share it.
output: Confirm the skill is broadly useful and contains no sensitive information.
Verify testing notes are ready before creating the contribution branch.
Prepare one focused pull request that includes only this skill.

output_examples.input: My pull request has merge conflicts.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends updating from upstream, resolving conflicts locally, and refreshing only your contribution branch after review.

output_examples.input: I am unsure if my skill is too project-specific.
output_examples.output: Keep it personal if it depends on private systems, internal policy, or narrow project context. Share generalized patterns only.

best_practices: Test the skill with the writing-skills process before preparing a pull request.
Review every command against your repository and remote names before running it.
Submit one skill per branch and pull request so maintainers can review it independently.
anti_patterns: Do not share skills that contain secrets, private URLs, or organization-specific procedures.
Do not batch unrelated skills into one pull request.
Do not force push without confirming you are updating only your contribution branch.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It guides you through submitting a tested skill to an upstream repository through a pull request.

faq.question: Does it create the skill content for me?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the skill already exists and has been tested.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Git and the GitHub CLI for branch, commit, push, and pull request steps.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code environments with shell access.

faq.question: Does it publish automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance, and you remain responsible for each repository command.

faq.question: What should I check before sharing?
faq.answer: Check for broad usefulness, clear documentation, completed tests, and absence of sensitive information.
